svg.title: Layered memory and execution defenses
svg.desc: A process address space shows randomized regions, non-executable writable pages, read-execute code, guard pages, stack canary and control-flow defenses.
svg.text: Memory defenses remove exploit assumptions; none repairs unsafe code
One randomized process address space
text + read-only data: R-X / R--
code can execute but not be modified
heap: RW-
writable data is non-executable
shared libraries / mmap: permissions per VMA
PIE and mapping bases vary across executions
guard page: PROT_NONE
stack: RW- + canary / protected return state
guard catches boundary crossing at page granularity
ASLR changes region bases and gaps
W^X / DEP / NX
A page should not be writable and executable at the same time.
JITs use controlled RW -> RX transitions, dual mappings, or a broker.
Goal: injected data is not immediately executable code.
ASLR + PIE
Randomize code, library, heap, stack and mapping locations.
Entropy raises reliability cost; information leaks can defeat it.
Randomization is probabilistic, not an authorization boundary.
Detection and control-flow hardening
Guard pages and canaries turn some corruption into early faults.
CFI, shadow stacks and pointer authentication protect control data.
Coverage and hardware/compiler support differ by platform.
Defense in depth changes exploitability; memory-safe code, validation, least privilege, sandboxing, patching and testing remain necessary.
